title: Countable-type nonarchimedean normed spaces have a separating bounded dual
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$. Let $V$ be a $k$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0$ exactly when $v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\le\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$. Suppose there is an at most countable set $D\subseteq V$ whose $k$-linear span is dense for the metric $d(v,w)=\|v-w\|$; this is the meaning of countable type. Then for every $0\ne v\in V$ there exist a $k$-linear map $h:V\to k$ and a real constant $C>0$ such that $h(v)\ne0$ and $|h(w)|\le C\|w\|$ for every $w\in V$. Completeness of $V$ and spherical completeness of $k$ are not assumed.

source.place: Definition 2.7.1/1 and Proposition 2.7.1/2, printed p.110 (scan PDF p.118), bounded-separation consequence; standing assumptions immediately above 2.7.1: k complete with nontrivial valuation. Primary scan read online 2026-10-25; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $v\ne0$. Enumerate a countable generating set of dense span, adjoining $v$ and padding finite sets by zero, as $(d_n)_{n\ge0}$. Put $U_n=\operatorname{span}_k(v,d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1})$, $c_n=(2-2^{-n})/\|v\|$, and $r_n=c_n/c_{n+1}\in(0,1)$. On $U_0=kv$ define $g_0(av)=a$. This is well-defined and linear, $g_0(v)=1$, and $|g_0(av)|=\|av\|/\|v\|=c_0\|av\|$.

source.place: Agent proof of the bounded-separation consequence of Proposition 2.7.1/2; archival copy absent, WANTED. Countable induction with controlled bounds, followed by dense extension.

proof.text: Inductively suppose $g_n:U_n\to k$ is linear, agrees with the earlier maps, takes $v$ to $1$, and satisfies $|g_n(u)|\le c_n\|u\|$. The finite spanning tuple makes $U_n$ finite-dimensional; it is closed in the Hausdorff norm topology by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed], since $k$ is complete and its absolute value nontrivial. If $d_n\notin U_n$, apply [lem-trf-ultrametric-one-vector-approximate-projection] to $U_n$, $d_n$ and $r_n$, obtaining $P_n:U_{n+1}\to U_n$. Define $g_{n+1}=g_n\circ P_n$. Then it extends $g_n$ and $|g_{n+1}(w)|\le c_n r_n^{-1}\|w\|=c_{n+1}\|w\|$. If $d_n\in U_n$, take $g_{n+1}=g_n$ on $U_{n+1}=U_n$ and use $c_n\le c_{n+1}$. This proves the inductive claim for every $n$.

source.place: Agent proof of the bounded-separation consequence of Proposition 2.7.1/2; archival copy absent, WANTED. Countable induction with controlled bounds, followed by dense extension.

proof.text: The increasing union $M=\bigcup_nU_n$ is a linear subspace: any two members lie in a common $U_n$. Define $g(w)=g_n(w)$ for any $n$ with $w\in U_n$; compatibility makes this independent of $n$ and linear by moving finite expressions to a common stage. All $d_n$ lie in $M$, so $M$ is dense. Also $g(v)=1$, and $c_n\le C:=2/\|v\|$ gives $|g(w)|\le C\|w\|$ for every $w\in M$, with $C>0$.

source.place: Agent proof of the bounded-separation consequence of Proposition 2.7.1/2; archival copy absent, WANTED. Countable induction with controlled bounds, followed by dense extension.

proof.text: Give $V$ the rescaled norm $N(w)=C\|w\|$. Since $C>0$, this is a definite homogeneous norm, and its balls are the original balls with radii divided by $C$; thus $M$ remains dense. On $M$, $|g(w)|\le N(w)$. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] with this norm and the complete codomain $k$. Its extension $h:V\to k$ is linear, agrees with $g$ on $M$, and satisfies $|h(w)|\le N(w)=C\|w\|$ on $V$. In particular $h(v)=g(v)=1\ne0$.
